newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds keep falling, volume thin.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds keep falling, volume thin.

text.p: Argentine bonds slipped again Thursday in thin volume in a cautious market focused on the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting next week, dealers said.
"The local market is scared," Alberto Lamm, broker for Banco Republica said.

"There are still fears of a possible U.S. rates hike and a possible long bond rate fall. Nevertheless neither local pension funds nor banks were heavy sellers because they still see a positive market."
The FRB fell 5/8 to 85-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 shed $0.21 to 121.59.
A foreign bank broker said prices are falling but amid low volume.
"Pension funds are scared, but nobody sells at current prices," he said.
"In case the Fed does not change rates, at these price levels bying pressure could arise. Uncertainty could start to spell out just after the Fed's meeting."
